prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Greenvale Metro: underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering-hour. Communications-Based Train Control system (CBTC): separation/authority/regulation. Line Traffic Controller coordinates service/recovery; Revenue Train Operator handles readiness/cab/passengers/instructions; Cyber Security Officer oversees access/security. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern) displays positions/zones/radio-alarms/supervision; sends Crew Login Token Bundle; no direct vital intervention. Voice Dispatch Console: degraded coordination, never substitutes safety messages/validation. Passenger Information Gateway distributes approved messages; Service Timetable Server supplies schedules; selected service outputs isolated from protection commands. North District Zone Controller (Marble): northern mainline/turnback/East Junction Interlocking (Falcon) approach. South District Zone Controller (Orchid): southern mainline/turnback/West Junction Interlocking approach. Controllers derive authority from location/occupancy/field-state. Transfer: ownership/overlap; receiving zone validates route/train/section before extension/reissue. North requests routes consistent with authority/approach; South checks flank/conflict protection. Interlockings report switch/occupancy/locking vitally; retain final point-movement/point-locking/route-locking/protected-section-release authority. Route availability requires points detected/locked/proved. Junction boundary uses route/point/vacancy, not chainage. Wayside compares indications/positions/radio; mismatches withhold/shorten authority until rule-compliant resolution. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel) validates authority sequence/applicability/consistency; protects speed/doors/commands. Activation requires authentication/energization/integrity. Modes: initialization/protected-manual/automatic-train/fallback/cutout. Recalculates braking each cycle; validated enforcement data yields Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer supplies speed/distance; confirms boundary position before source acceptance; divergence increases uncertainty/separation requests. Propulsion/braking interface isolates non-vital inputs; assurance checks feedback/pressure/deceleration. Operator interface rejects stale/inconsistent acknowledgements. Train Radio Modem uses Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron): overlapping coverage; reports quality/registration/continuity before minimum margin; prefers checked make-before-break. Degradation retains last validated authority. Network sends Radio Handover Audit File each configured interval. Safety Data Communication Network: deterministic/authenticated/integrity-checked/bounded-monitored-latency vital transport, non-vital separation; sends Clock Drift Sample Report each synchronization

Document units:
S083: A requested route is not incorporated into a movement authority until the associated overlap and flank conditions are confirmed as protected.
S084: If the interlocking reports loss of point correspondence after a route has been granted, the affected movement authority is shortened or withdrawn according to the safe braking envelope.
S085: Axle counter clear and occupied indications are used as independent wayside evidence for route availability and for the continued integrity of route locking.
S086: Where axle counter occupation conflicts with the train location estimated by the CBTC system, the more restrictive state is applied until the discrepancy is resolved.
S087: East Junction Interlocking sends the Axle Counter Reset Request under the configured degraded-mode reset procedure.
S088: Reset processing is inhibited while any associated route remains locked or while a train is approaching the affected detection section.
S089: Maple verifies local track clearance evidence and records the result before authorising restoration of normal route setting after a detection anomaly.
S090: West Junction Interlocking sends the Route Release Exception List when normal sectional release cannot be completed within the configured timing rules.
S091: The zone controller treats any release exception as a retained hazard until the affected path is excluded from new movement authorities.
S092: Platform approach protection is enforced by combining the active route state with train stopping accuracy supervision near the platform berth.
S093: The Platform Screen Door Controller provides door closed and locked indications to the supervising wayside systems, but those indications do not replace interlocking route proof.
S094: If platform door readiness is absent, the approaching train may be held outside the platform stopping window even when the junction route is otherwise proved.
S095: The Atlas Onboard Controller uses the token bundle to validate that onboard operating context is current before accepting supervised route-related data.
S096: Train Radio Modem messages carrying route status are exchanged through Wayside Radio Access Network paths with sequence monitoring and timeout handling.
S097: Safety Data Communication Network paths between the zone controllers and the interlockings are configured for deterministic delivery of vital state changes and command acknowledgements.
S098: Metro Operations Control System displays the commanded route, locked route, point state, and track occupancy state as separate indications so that control staff can identify mismatches.
S099: A Line Traffic Controller may request a regulating action, but the request is executed only if the interlocking and CBTC protection rules agree that the route remains safe.
S100: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server records route command outcomes, point operation timing, and detection transitions for later engineering review without participating in vital decisions.
